description:
FILED s519b (Opus 5.5, s520, 2026-10-18) from the IO-Compress board census: an EMBEDDED `my` in the RIGHT side of a `my` declaration, inside a loop body, is not let-bound per iteration -- it is the file-level cell, so it keeps the value an earlier iteration (or an aliasing callee) wrote.  SILENT WRONG (PRE-EXISTING: same on fca3593b).

REPRO:
  sub X::n { shift; foreach (@_) { print defined $_ ? "D " : "U "; $_ = "y" } }
  for my $k (1..2) { my $l = X->n(my $t); print "$k $t\n" }
perl: U 1 y / U 2 y.   PCL: U 1 y / D 2 y.
Without the outer `my $l =` (`X->n(my $u);` as a statement) PCL agrees with perl: the statement-level lowering binds `$u` with (p-let (($u :box ...))), but `(p-my-= $l (... (p-method-call ... $t)))` reads `$t` as the file cell (p-defcell $t) -- no per-iteration binding.

REACH: IO-Compress t/compress/CompTestUtils.pm `my $lex = LexFile->new( my $name );` in loops -- LexFile::new croaks "NO!!!!" when its argument is defined, which kills the file: 002any-transparent, 005defhdr, 006zip, 010examples-zlib, 011-streamzip, 01misc, 050interop-gzip, 100generic-*, 102tied-*, 103newtied-*, ... (the s519b board join rows citing #3431).  Probe file: scratch/s519b/pr2/lex3.pl in the s519b worktree.
subject: SILENT WRONG: an embedded `my` in the RHS of a `my` declaration inside a loop (`my $l = X->n(my $t)`) is the file cell, not a per-iteration lexical -- IO-Compress LexFile->new(my $name) croaks NO!!!!
